style: Modern pixel art with soft lighting (Style D): a small translucent glowing blue jelly slime, soft inner glow, gentle highlights, a clean dark-blue outline, chunky readable pixels, two small glossy dark eyes. Match the character, colours and proportions of the reference images exactly. Side view, the slime facing right.

frames.name: idle_1
frames.prompt: The slime resting: a rounded dome slightly wider than tall, two eyes near the upper front (right), relaxed.

frames.name: idle_2
frames.prompt: The same slime breathing out: very slightly flatter and wider (about 5 percent squash), same eyes and colours.

frames.name: run_1
frames.prompt: The same slime mid-run: leaning forward to the right and stretched slightly horizontally, the back trailing, eyes looking right.

frames.name: run_2
frames.prompt: The same slime in the run's recovery: compressed and a little taller, hunched, bouncing up.

frames.name: run_3
frames.prompt: The same slime stretched forward again like the first run frame, with the trailing back edge pulled in a little.

frames.name: run_4
frames.prompt: The same slime compressed and popping up slightly higher than the resting pose.

frames.name: rise
frames.prompt: The same slime jumping upward: only moderately stretched, about 25 percent taller than the resting dome and a little narrower, with a soft rounded top like a tall egg. No point, no cone, no spike on top. Eyes wide.

frames.name: fall
frames.prompt: The same slime falling: about 15 percent taller than the resting dome, a smooth rounded dome with a slightly wider bottom. No horns, no ears, no points anywhere on the outline. Eyes wide.

frames.name: land
frames.prompt: The same slime landing: squashed very flat and wide, eyes squinting.

frames.name: hurt
frames.prompt: The same slime hit and recoiling: squashed sideways with a slight tilt, eyes squeezed shut in pain.

frames.name: rope
frames.prompt: The same slime hanging from a thread by a small point on top of its head, like a soft water balloon being lifted: its body is full and rounded like an egg standing on its narrow end, about one and a third times as tall as it is wide, widest near the bottom, the top gently rounded (never a sharp spike or a teardrop point) with only a tiny soft nub at the very top centre. Eyes open, looking forward, in the middle of the body. Do not draw any thread, rope or line: the nub is the top of the sprite.

frames.name: wall_1
frames.prompt: The same slime clinging to a wall on its RIGHT side: its front edge pressed flat against the wall, two small jelly arms gripping upward on the right, eyes looking up.

frames.name: wall_2
frames.prompt: The same clinging pose with the grip shifted: the arms a little lower, the body slightly stretched downward.

frames.name: tackle
frames.prompt: The same slime in a charging tackle: stretched long horizontally with a leading edge pointing forward to the right, streamlined, eyes narrowed and determined.

frames.name: spread_1
frames.prompt: The same slime half flattened, squashing down into a puddle: wider and lower than resting, eyes near the top.

frames.name: spread_2
frames.prompt: The same slime fully spread into a flat puddle: very wide, low and thin like a pancake, the eyes as two tiny ovals on the top edge.

frames.name: cover_1
frames.prompt: The same slime lunging: its body arching up and forward to the right like a leap over something, eyes looking down and to the right.

frames.name: cover_2
frames.prompt: The same slime draping down like a blanket over something below it: a wide low mound with its edges spreading out to the sides, pale glowing blue.

frames.name: cover_3
frames.prompt: The same slime engulfing something: a wide flat mound with its edges hugging the ground on both sides, glowing, a hollow dark shape suggested inside.

frames.name: cover_4
frames.prompt: The same engulfing pose pulsing slightly bigger, its edges spread a little more.

frames.name: cover_5
frames.prompt: The same slime popping back into a round dome after eating, happy eyes, nothing else in the frame (no sparkles, no droplets).
